audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 2, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal witness audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for masculinity commands, David's deathbed revenge instructions, Abishag as dynastic property, sanctuary execution, priestly removal, confinement, escaped servants, oath enforcement, and consolidation through killing.

verses.restored: Days of David drew near to die, and he commanded Solomon his son, saying:

familiar.text: Now the days of David drew nigh that he should die; and he charged Solomon his son, saying,

modern.text: As the time drew near for David to die, he charged his son Solomon,

original.text: וַיִּקְרְב֥וּ יְמֵֽי דָוִ֖ד לָמ֑וּת וַיְצַ֛ו אֶת שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: I am going way of all earth. Be strong, and become a man.

familiar.text: I go the way of all the earth: be thou strong therefore, and shew thyself a man;

modern.text: “I am about to go the way of all the earth. So be strong and prove yourself a man.

original.text: אָנֹכִ֣י הֹלֵ֔ךְ בְּדֶ֖רֶךְ כָּל הָאָ֑רֶץ וְחָזַקְתָּ֖ וְהָיִ֥יתָֽ לְאִֽישׁ

verses.restored: Keep charge of YHWH your Divine: walk in YHWH's ways, keep statutes, commands, judgments, and testimonies, as written in Torah of Moses, so you may act wisely/prosper in all you do and wherever you turn.

familiar.text: And keep the charge of the LORD thy God, to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, and his commandments, and his judgments, and his testimonies, as it is written in the law of Moses, that thou mayest prosper in all that thou doest, and whithersoever thou turnest thyself:

modern.text: And keep the charge of the LORD your God to walk in His ways and to keep His statutes, commandments, ordinances, and decrees, as is written in the Law of Moses, so that you may prosper in all you do and wherever you turn,

original.text: וְשָׁמַרְתָּ֞ אֶת מִשְׁמֶ֣רֶת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ לָלֶ֤כֶת בִּדְרָכָיו֙ לִשְׁמֹ֨ר חֻקֹּתָ֤יו מִצְוֺתָיו֙ וּמִשְׁפָּטָ֣יו וְעֵדְוֺתָ֔יו כַּכָּת֖וּב בְּתוֹרַ֣ת מֹשֶׁ֑ה לְמַ֣עַן תַּשְׂכִּ֗יל אֵ֚ת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּֽעֲשֶׂ֔ה וְאֵ֛ת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּפְנֶ֖ה שָֽׁם

verses.restored: So YHWH may establish word spoken concerning me: If your children guard their way, walking before me in faithfulness with all heart and soul, no man shall be cut off for you from throne of Israel.

familiar.text: That the LORD may continue his word which he spake concerning me, saying, If thy children take heed to their way, to walk before me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul, there shall not fail thee (said he) a man on the throne of Israel.

modern.text: and so that the LORD may fulfill His promise to me: ‘If your descendants take heed to walk faithfully before Me with all their heart and soul, you will never fail to have a man on the throne of Israel.’

original.text: לְמַעַן֩ יָקִ֨ים יְהוָ֜ה אֶת דְּבָר֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֣ר עָלַי֮ לֵאמֹר֒ אִם יִשְׁמְר֨וּ בָנֶ֜יךָ אֶת דַּרְכָּ֗ם לָלֶ֤כֶת לְפָנַי֙ בֶּאֱמֶ֔ת בְּכָל לְבָבָ֖ם וּבְכָל נַפְשָׁ֑ם לֵאמֹ֕ר לֹֽא יִכָּרֵ֤ת לְךָ֙ אִ֔ישׁ מֵעַ֖ל כִּסֵּ֥א יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: You also know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me—what he did to two commanders of armies of Israel, Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether. He killed them and placed blood of war in peace upon belt at his waist and sandals on his feet.

familiar.text: Moreover thou knowest also what Joab the son of Zeruiah did to me, and what he did to the two captains of the hosts of Israel, unto Abner the son of Ner, and unto Amasa the son of Jether, whom he slew, and shed the blood of war in peace, and put the blood of war upon his girdle that was about his loins, and in his shoes that were on his feet.

modern.text: Moreover, you know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me—what he did to Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether, the two commanders of the armies of Israel. He killed them in peacetime to avenge the blood of war. He stained with the blood of war the belt around his waist and the sandals on his feet.

original.text: וְגַ֣ם אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֡עְתָּ אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁר עָ֨שָׂה לִ֜י יוֹאָ֣ב בֶּן צְרוּיָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֣ה לִשְׁנֵֽי שָׂרֵ֣י צִבְא֣וֹת יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל לְאַבְנֵ֨ר בֶּן נֵ֜ר וְלַעֲמָשָׂ֤א בֶן יֶ֨תֶר֙ וַיַּ֣הַרְגֵ֔ם וַיָּ֥שֶׂם דְּמֵֽי מִלְחָמָ֖ה בְּשָׁלֹ֑ם וַיִּתֵּ֞ן דְּמֵ֣י מִלְחָמָ֗ה בַּחֲגֹֽרָתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּמָתְנָ֔יו וּֽבְנַעֲל֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּרַגְלָֽיו

verses.restored: Act according to your wisdom, and do not let his gray head go down to Sheol in peace.

familiar.text: Do therefore according to thy wisdom, and let not his hoar head go down to the grave in peace.

modern.text: So act according to your wisdom, and do not let his gray head go down to Sheol in peace.

original.text: וְעָשִׂ֖יתָ כְּחָכְמָתֶ֑ךָ וְלֹֽא תוֹרֵ֧ד שֵׂיבָת֛וֹ בְּשָׁלֹ֖ם שְׁאֹֽל

verses.restored: But show covenant-kindness to sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be among those eating at your table, because they came near to me when I fled from Absalom your brother.

familiar.text: But shew kindness unto the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be of those that eat at thy table: for so they came to me when I fled because of Absalom thy brother.

modern.text: But show loving devotion to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be among those who eat at your table, because they stood by me when I fled from your brother Absalom.

original.text: וְלִבְנֵ֨י בַרְזִלַּ֤י הַגִּלְעָדִי֙ תַּֽעֲשֶׂה חֶ֔סֶד וְהָי֖וּ בְּאֹכְלֵ֣י שֻׁלְחָנֶ֑ךָ כִּי כֵן֙ קָרְב֣וּ אֵלַ֔י בְּבָרְחִ֕י מִפְּנֵ֖י אַבְשָׁל֥וֹם אָחִֽיךָ

verses.restored: Look, with you is Shimei son of Gera, Benjaminite from Bahurim, who cursed me with a grievous curse on day I went to Mahanaim. But he came down to meet me at Jordan, and I swore to him by YHWH, saying, I will not put you to death with sword.

familiar.text: And, behold, thou hast with thee Shimei the son of Gera, a Benjamite of Bahurim, which cursed me with a grievous curse in the day when I went to Mahanaim: but he came down to meet me at Jordan, and I sware to him by the LORD, saying, I will not put thee to death with the sword.

modern.text: Keep an eye on Shimei the son of Gera, the Benjamite from Bahurim who is with you. He called down bitter curses against me on the day I went to Mahanaim, but when he came down to meet me at the Jordan, I swore to him by the LORD: ‘I will never put you to the sword.’

original.text: וְהִנֵּ֣ה עִ֠מְּךָ שִֽׁמְעִ֨י בֶן גֵּרָ֥א בֶן הַיְמִינִי֮ מִבַּחֻרִים֒ וְה֤וּא קִֽלְלַ֨נִי֙ קְלָלָ֣ה נִמְרֶ֔צֶת בְּי֖וֹם לֶכְתִּ֣י מַחֲנָ֑יִם וְהֽוּא יָרַ֤ד לִקְרָאתִי֙ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וָאֶשָּׁ֨בַֽע ל֤וֹ בַֽיהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אִם אֲמִֽיתְךָ֖ בֶּחָֽרֶב

verses.restored: Now do not hold him guiltless, for you are a wise man and know what you should do to him. Bring his gray head down to Sheol with blood.

familiar.text: Now therefore hold him not guiltless: for thou art a wise man, and knowest what thou oughtest to do unto him; but his hoar head bring thou down to the grave with blood.

modern.text: Now therefore, do not hold him guiltless, for you are a wise man. You know what you ought to do to him to bring his gray head down to Sheol in blood.” David’s Reign and Death (1 Chronicles 29:26–30)

original.text: וְעַתָּה֙ אַל תְּנַקֵּ֔הוּ כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ חָכָ֖ם אָ֑תָּה וְיָֽדַעְתָּ֙ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּֽעֲשֶׂה לּ֔וֹ וְהוֹרַדְתָּ֧ אֶת שֵׂיבָת֛וֹ בְּדָ֖ם שְׁאֽוֹל

verses.restored: David lay with his ancestors and was buried in City of David.

familiar.text: So David slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David.

modern.text: Then David rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב דָּוִ֖ד עִם אֲבֹתָ֑יו וַיִּקָּבֵ֖ר בְּעִ֥יר דָּוִֽד

verses.restored: Days David reigned over Israel were forty years: seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And the days that David reigned over Israel were forty years: seven years reigned he in Hebron, and thirty and three years reigned he in Jerusalem.

modern.text: The length of David’s reign over Israel was forty years—seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.

original.text: וְהַיָּמִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר מָלַ֤ךְ דָּוִד֙ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה בְּחֶבְר֤וֹן מָלַךְ֙ שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֔ים וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֣ם מָלַ֔ךְ שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וְשָׁלֹ֖שׁ שָׁנִֽים

verses.restored: Solomon sat upon throne of David his father, and his kingdom was firmly established.

familiar.text: Then sat Solomon upon the throne of David his father; and his kingdom was established greatly.

modern.text: So Solomon sat on the throne of his father David, and his kingdom was firmly established. The Execution of Adonijah

original.text: וּשְׁלֹמֹ֕ה יָשַׁ֕ב עַל כִּסֵּ֖א דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יו וַתִּכֹּ֥ן מַלְכֻת֖וֹ מְאֹֽד

verses.restored: Adonijah son of Haggith came to Bathsheba, mother of Solomon. She said, Do you come in peace? He said, In peace.

familiar.text: And Adonijah the son of Haggith came to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon. And she said, Comest thou peaceably? And he said, Peaceably.

modern.text: Now Adonijah son of Haggith went to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, and she asked, “Do you come in peace?” “Yes, in peace,” he replied.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֞א אֲדֹנִיָּ֣הוּ בֶן חַגֵּ֗ית אֶל בַּת שֶׁ֨בַע֙ אֵם שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וַתֹּ֖אמֶר הֲשָׁל֣וֹם בֹּאֶ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר שָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: He said, I have a word for you. She said, Speak.

familiar.text: He said moreover, I have somewhat to say unto thee. And she said, Say on.

modern.text: Then he said, “I have something to tell you.” “Say it,” she answered.

original.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר דָּבָ֥ר לִ֖י אֵלָ֑יִךְ וַתֹּ֖אמֶר דַּבֵּֽר

verses.restored: He said, You know kingdom was mine and all Israel set faces toward me to reign. But kingdom turned and became my brother's, for it was his from YHWH.

familiar.text: And he said, Thou knowest that the kingdom was mine, and that all Israel set their faces on me, that I should reign: howbeit the kingdom is turned about, and is become my brother’s: for it was his from the LORD.

modern.text: “You know that the kingship was mine,” he said. “All Israel expected that I should reign, but the kingship has turned to my brother, for it has come to him from the LORD.

original.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אַ֤תְּ יָדַ֨עַתְּ֙ כִּי לִי֙ הָיְתָ֣ה הַמְּלוּכָ֔ה וְעָלַ֞י שָׂ֧מוּ כָֽל יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל פְּנֵיהֶ֖ם לִמְלֹ֑ךְ וַתִּסֹּ֤ב הַמְּלוּכָה֙ וַתְּהִ֣י לְאָחִ֔י כִּ֥י מֵיְהוָ֖ה הָ֥יְתָה לּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Now I ask one request from you; do not turn my face away. She said, Speak.

familiar.text: And now I ask one petition of thee, deny me not. And she said unto him, Say on.

modern.text: So now I have just one request of you; do not deny me.” “State your request,” she told him.

original.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה שְׁאֵלָ֤ה אַחַת֙ אָֽנֹכִי֙ שֹׁאֵ֣ל מֵֽאִתָּ֔ךְ אַל תָּשִׁ֖בִי אֶת פָּנָ֑י וַתֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלָ֖יו דַּבֵּֽר

verses.restored: He said, Please speak to Solomon the king—for he will not turn you away—that he give me Abishag the Shunammite as wife.

familiar.text: And he said, Speak, I pray thee, unto Solomon the king, (for he will not say thee nay,) that he give me Abishag the Shunammite to wife.

modern.text: Adonijah replied, “Please speak to King Solomon, since he will not turn you down. Let him give me Abishag the Shunammite as my wife.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אִמְרִי נָא֙ לִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּ֥י לֹֽא יָשִׁ֖יב אֶת פָּנָ֑יִךְ וְיִתֶּן לִ֛י אֶת אֲבִישַׁ֥ג הַשּׁוּנַמִּ֖ית לְאִשָּֽׁה

verses.restored: Bathsheba said, Good; I will speak for you to king.

familiar.text: And Bathsheba said, Well; I will speak for thee unto the king.

modern.text: “Very well,” Bathsheba replied. “I will speak to the king for you.”

original.text: וַתֹּ֥אמֶר בַּת שֶׁ֖בַע ט֑וֹב אָנֹכִ֕י אֲדַבֵּ֥ר עָלֶ֖יךָ אֶל הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Bathsheba came to King Solomon to speak for Adonijah. The king rose to meet her, bowed to her, sat upon throne, and set a throne for mother of king; she sat at his right hand.

familiar.text: Bathsheba therefore went unto king Solomon, to speak unto him for Adonijah. And the king rose up to meet her, and bowed himself unto her, and sat down on his throne, and caused a seat to be set for the king’s mother; and she sat on his right hand.

modern.text: So Bathsheba went to King Solomon to speak to him for Adonijah. The king stood up to greet her, bowed to her, and sat down on his throne. Then the king had a throne brought for his mother, who sat down at his right hand.

original.text: וַתָּבֹ֤א בַת שֶׁ֨בַע֙ אֶל הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה לְדַבֶּר ל֖וֹ עַל אֲדֹנִיָּ֑הוּ וַיָּקָם֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ לִקְרָאתָ֜הּ וַיִּשְׁתַּ֣חוּ לָ֗הּ וַיֵּ֨שֶׁב֙ עַל כִּסְא֔וֹ וַיָּ֤שֶׂם כִּסֵּא֙ לְאֵ֣ם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַתֵּ֖שֶׁב לִֽימִינֽוֹ

verses.restored: She said, I ask one small request from you; do not turn my face away. The king said, Ask, my mother, for I will not turn you away.

familiar.text: Then she said, I desire one small petition of thee; I pray thee, say me not nay. And the king said unto her, Ask on, my mother: for I will not say thee nay.

modern.text: “I have just one small request of you,” she said. “Do not deny me.” “Make your request, my mother,” the king replied, “for I will not deny you.”

original.text: וַתֹּ֗אמֶר שְׁאֵלָ֨ה אַחַ֤ת קְטַנָּה֙ אָֽנֹכִי֙ שֹׁאֶ֣לֶת מֵֽאִתָּ֔ךְ אַל תָּ֖שֶׁב אֶת פָּנָ֑י וַיֹּֽאמֶר לָ֤הּ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ שַׁאֲלִ֣י אִמִּ֔י כִּ֥י לֹֽא אָשִׁ֖יב אֶת פָּנָֽיִךְ

verses.restored: She said, Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to Adonijah your brother as wife.

familiar.text: And she said, Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to Adonijah thy brother to wife.

modern.text: So Bathsheba said, “Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to your brother Adonijah as his wife.”

original.text: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר יֻתַּ֖ן אֶת אֲבִישַׁ֣ג הַשֻּׁנַמִּ֑ית לַאֲדֹנִיָּ֥הוּ אָחִ֖יךָ לְאִשָּֽׁה

verses.restored: King Solomon answered his mother, Why do you ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask for him kingdom also, for he is my older brother—and for him, Abiathar the priest, and Joab son of Zeruiah.

familiar.text: And king Solomon answered and said unto his mother, And why dost thou ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? ask for him the kingdom also; for he is mine elder brother; even for him, and for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab the son of Zeruiah.

modern.text: King Solomon answered his mother, “Why do you request Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Since he is my older brother, you might as well request the kingdom for him and for Abiathar the priest and for Joab son of Zeruiah!”

original.text: וַיַּעַן֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְאִמּ֗וֹ וְלָמָה֩ אַ֨תְּ שֹׁאֶ֜לֶת אֶת אֲבִישַׁ֤ג הַשֻּׁנַמִּית֙ לַאֲדֹ֣נִיָּ֔הוּ וְשַֽׁאֲלִי לוֹ֙ אֶת הַמְּלוּכָ֔ה כִּ֛י ה֥וּא אָחִ֖י הַגָּד֣וֹל מִמֶּ֑נִּי וְלוֹ֙ וּלְאֶבְיָתָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וּלְיוֹאָ֖ב בֶּן צְרוּיָֽה

verses.restored: King Solomon swore by YHWH, saying, Thus may Divine do to me and thus add, if Adonijah did not speak this word against his own life.

familiar.text: Then king Solomon sware by the LORD, saying, God do so to me, and more also, if Adonijah have not spoken this word against his own life.

modern.text: Then King Solomon swore by the LORD: “May God punish me, and ever so severely, if Adonijah has not made this request at the expense of his life.

original.text: וַיִּשָּׁבַע֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה בַּֽיהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר כֹּ֣ה יַֽעֲשֶׂה לִּ֤י אֱלֹהִים֙ וְכֹ֣ה יוֹסִ֔יף כִּ֣י בְנַפְשׁ֔וֹ דִּבֶּר֙ אֲדֹ֣נִיָּ֔הוּ אֶת הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Now, as YHWH lives, who established me, seated me upon throne of David my father, and made me a house as promised, Adonijah shall be put to death this day.

familiar.text: Now therefore, as the LORD liveth, which hath established me, and set me on the throne of David my father, and who hath made me an house, as he promised, Adonijah shall be put to death this day.

modern.text: And now, as surely as the LORD lives—the One who established me, who set me on the throne of my father David, and who founded for me a dynasty as He promised—surely Adonijah shall be put to death today!”

original.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה חַי יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֱכִינַ֗נִי ויושיביני עַל כִּסֵּא֙ דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֔י וַאֲשֶׁ֧ר עָֽשָׂה לִ֛י בַּ֖יִת כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֵּ֑ר כִּ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם יוּמַ֖ת אֲדֹנִיָּֽהוּ

verses.restored: King Solomon sent by hand of Benaiah son of Jehoiada. He struck Adonijah, and he died.

familiar.text: And king Solomon sent by the hand of Benaiah the son of Jehoiada; and he fell upon him that he died.

modern.text: So King Solomon sent the order to Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who struck down Adonijah, and he died.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה בְּיַ֖ד בְּנָיָ֣הוּ בֶן יְהוֹיָדָ֑ע וַיִּפְגַּע בּ֖וֹ וַיָּמֹֽת

verses.restored: To Abiathar the priest the king said, Go to Anathoth, to your fields, for you are a man of death. But this day I will not put you to death, because you carried ark of Lord YHWH before David my father and were afflicted in all my father was afflicted.

familiar.text: And unto Abiathar the priest said the king, Get thee to Anathoth, unto thine own fields; for thou art worthy of death: but I will not at this time put thee to death, because thou barest the ark of the LORD God before David my father, and because thou hast been afflicted in all wherein my father was afflicted.

modern.text: Then the king said to Abiathar the priest, “Go back to your fields in Anathoth. Even though you deserve to die, I will not put you to death at this time, since you carried the ark of the Lord GOD before my father David, and you suffered through all that my father suffered.”

original.text: וּלְאֶבְיָתָ֨ר הַכֹּהֵ֜ן אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ עֲנָתֹת֙ לֵ֣ךְ עַל שָׂדֶ֔יךָ כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ מָ֖וֶת אָ֑תָּה וּבַיּ֨וֹם הַזֶּ֜ה לֹ֣א אֲמִיתֶ֗ךָ כִּֽי נָשָׂ֜אתָ אֶת אֲר֨וֹן אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהֹוִה֙ לִפְנֵי֙ דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֔י וְכִ֣י הִתְעַנִּ֔יתָ בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶֽׁר הִתְעַנָּ֖ה אָבִֽי

verses.restored: Solomon expelled Abiathar from being priest to YHWH, fulfilling word of YHWH spoken concerning house of Eli in Shiloh.

familiar.text: So Solomon thrust out Abiathar from being priest unto the LORD; that he might fulfil the word of the LORD, which he spake concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh.

modern.text: So Solomon banished Abiathar from the priesthood of the LORD and thus fulfilled the word that the LORD had spoken at Shiloh against the house of Eli. The Execution of Joab

original.text: וַיְגָ֤רֶשׁ שְׁלֹמֹה֙ אֶת אֶבְיָתָ֔ר מִהְי֥וֹת כֹּהֵ֖ן לַֽיהוָ֑ה לְמַלֵּא֙ אֶת דְּבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּ֛ר עַל בֵּ֥ית עֵלִ֖י בְּשִׁלֹֽה

verses.restored: Report came to Joab, for Joab had turned after Adonijah, though not after Absalom. Joab fled to tent of YHWH and grasped horns of altar.

familiar.text: Then tidings came to Joab: for Joab had turned after Adonijah, though he turned not after Absalom. And Joab fled unto the tabernacle of the LORD, and caught hold on the horns of the altar.

modern.text: When the news reached Joab, who had conspired with Adonijah but not with Absalom, he fled to the tent of the LORD and took hold of the horns of the altar.

original.text: וְהַשְּׁמֻעָה֙ בָּ֣אָה עַד יוֹאָ֔ב כִּ֣י יוֹאָ֗ב נָטָה֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י אֲדֹנִיָּ֔ה וְאַחֲרֵ֥י אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם לֹ֣א נָטָ֑ה וַיָּ֤נָס יוֹאָב֙ אֶל אֹ֣הֶל יְהוָ֔ה וַֽיַּחֲזֵ֖ק בְּקַרְנ֥וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ

verses.restored: It was told King Solomon that Joab fled to tent of YHWH and was beside altar. Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying, Go, strike him.

familiar.text: And it was told king Solomon that Joab was fled unto the tabernacle of the LORD; and, behold, he is by the altar. Then Solomon sent Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, saying, Go, fall upon him.

modern.text: It was reported to King Solomon: “Joab has fled to the tent of the LORD and is now beside the altar.” So Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying, “Go, strike him down!”

original.text: וַיֻּגַּ֞ד לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה כִּ֣י נָ֤ס יוֹאָב֙ אֶל אֹ֣הֶל יְהוָ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֖ה אֵ֣צֶל הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה אֶת בְּנָיָ֧הוּ בֶן יְהוֹיָדָ֛ע לֵאמֹ֖ר לֵ֥ךְ פְּגַע בּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Benaiah came to tent of YHWH and said, Thus says king: Come out. Joab said, No, for here I will die. Benaiah returned word to king, saying, Thus Joab spoke and thus he answered me.

familiar.text: And Benaiah came to the tabernacle of the LORD, and said unto him, Thus saith the king, Come forth. And he said, Nay; but I will die here. And Benaiah brought the king word again, saying, Thus said Joab, and thus he answered me.

modern.text: And Benaiah entered the tent of the LORD and said to Joab, “The king says, ‘Come out!’” But Joab replied, “No, I will die here.” So Benaiah relayed the message to the king, saying, “This is how Joab answered me.”

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֨א בְנָיָ֜הוּ אֶל אֹ֣הֶל יְהוָ֗ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ צֵ֔א וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לֹ֖א כִּ֣י פֹ֣ה אָמ֑וּת וַיָּ֨שֶׁב בְּנָיָ֤הוּ אֶת הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ דָּבָ֣ר לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּֽה דִבֶּ֥ר יוֹאָ֖ב וְכֹ֥ה עָנָֽנִי

verses.restored: The king said, Do as he said: strike him and bury him, and remove from me and house of my father innocent blood Joab shed.

familiar.text: And the king said unto him, Do as he hath said, and fall upon him, and bury him; that thou mayest take away the innocent blood, which Joab shed, from me, and from the house of my father.

modern.text: And the king replied, “Do just as he says. Strike him down and bury him, and so remove from me and from the house of my father the innocent blood that Joab shed.

verses.restored: YHWH shall return his blood upon his head, because he struck two men more righteous and better than he and killed them with sword without David my father knowing: Abner son of Ner, commander of army of Israel, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of army of Judah.

familiar.text: And the LORD shall return his blood upon his own head, who fell upon two men more righteous and better than he, and slew them with the sword, my father David not knowing thereof, to wit, Abner the son of Ner, captain of the host of Israel, and Amasa the son of Jether, captain of the host of Judah.

modern.text: The LORD will bring his bloodshed back upon his own head, for without the knowledge of my father David he struck down two men more righteous and better than he when he put to the sword Abner son of Ner, commander of Israel’s army, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of Judah’s army.

original.text: וְהֵשִׁיב֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֶת דָּמ֜וֹ עַל רֹאשׁ֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר פָּגַ֣ע בִּשְׁנֵֽי אֲ֠נָשִׁים צַדִּקִ֨ים וְטֹבִ֤ים מִמֶּ֨נּוּ֙ וַיַּהַרְגֵ֣ם בַּחֶ֔רֶב וְאָבִ֥י דָוִ֖ד לֹ֣א יָדָ֑ע אֶת אַבְנֵ֤ר בֶּן נֵר֙ שַׂר צְבָ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאֶת עֲמָשָׂ֥א בֶן יֶ֖תֶר שַׂר צְבָ֥א יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: Their blood shall return upon head of Joab and head of his seed forever; but for David, his seed, his house, and his throne may there be peace forever from YHWH.

familiar.text: Their blood shall therefore return upon the head of Joab, and upon the head of his seed for ever: but upon David, and upon his seed, and upon his house, and upon his throne, shall there be peace for ever from the LORD.

modern.text: Their blood will come back upon the heads of Joab and his descendants forever; but for David, his descendants, his house, and his throne, there shall be peace from the LORD forever.”

original.text: וְשָׁ֤בוּ דְמֵיהֶם֙ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ יוֹאָ֔ב וּבְרֹ֥אשׁ זַרְע֖וֹ לְעֹלָ֑ם וּלְדָוִ֡ד וּ֠לְזַרְעוֹ וּלְבֵית֨וֹ וּלְכִסְא֜וֹ יִהְיֶ֥ה שָׁל֛וֹם עַד עוֹלָ֖ם מֵעִ֥ם יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up, struck him, and killed him. He was buried at his house in wilderness.

familiar.text: So Benaiah the son of Jehoiada went up, and fell upon him, and slew him: and he was buried in his own house in the wilderness.

modern.text: So Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up, struck down Joab, and killed him. He was buried at his own home in the wilderness.

original.text: וַיַּ֗עַל בְּנָיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן יְה֣וֹיָדָ֔ע וַיִּפְגַּע בּ֖וֹ וַיְמִתֵ֑הוּ וַיִּקָּבֵ֥ר בְּבֵית֖וֹ בַּמִּדְבָּֽר

verses.restored: The king placed Benaiah son of Jehoiada over army in his place, and Zadok the priest the king placed in place of Abiathar.

familiar.text: And the king put Benaiah the son of Jehoiada in his room over the host: and Zadok the priest did the king put in the room of Abiathar.

modern.text: And the king appointed Benaiah son of Jehoiada in Joab’s place over the army, and he appointed Zadok the priest in Abiathar’s place. The Execution of Shimei

verses.restored: The king sent and called Shimei and said, Build for yourself a house in Jerusalem and live there; do not go out from there anywhere.

familiar.text: And the king sent and called for Shimei, and said unto him, Build thee an house in Jerusalem, and dwell there, and go not forth thence any whither.

modern.text: Then the king summoned Shimei and said to him, “Build a house for yourself in Jerusalem and live there, but do not go anywhere else.

verses.restored: On day you go out and cross wadi Kidron, know surely that dying you shall die; your blood shall be upon your own head.

familiar.text: For it shall be, that on the day thou goest out, and passest over the brook Kidron, thou shalt know for certain that thou shalt surely die: thy blood shall be upon thine own head.

modern.text: On the day you go out and cross the Kidron Valley, know for sure that you will die; your blood will be on your own head.”

verses.restored: Shimei said to king, The word is good. As my lord the king has spoken, so your servant will do. Shimei lived in Jerusalem many days.

familiar.text: And Shimei said unto the king, The saying is good: as my lord the king hath said, so will thy servant do. And Shimei dwelt in Jerusalem many days.

modern.text: “The sentence is fair,” Shimei replied. “Your servant will do as my lord the king has spoken.” And Shimei lived in Jerusalem for a long time.

verses.restored: At end of three years, two servants/slaves of Shimei fled to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. They told Shimei, Look, your servants are in Gath.

familiar.text: And it came to pass at the end of three years, that two of the servants of Shimei ran away unto Achish son of Maachah king of Gath. And they told Shimei, saying, Behold, thy servants be in Gath.

modern.text: After three years, however, two of Shimei’s slaves ran away to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. And Shimei was told, “Look, your slaves are in Gath.”

familiar.text: And Shimei arose, and saddled his ass, and went to Gath to Achish to seek his servants: and Shimei went, and brought his servants from Gath.

modern.text: So Shimei saddled his donkey and set out to Achish at Gath in search of his slaves, and he brought them back from Gath.

verses.restored: It was told Solomon that Shimei went from Jerusalem to Gath and returned.

familiar.text: And it was told Solomon that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath, and was come again.

modern.text: When Solomon was told that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and had returned,

verses.restored: The king sent and called Shimei and said, Did I not make you swear by YHWH and warn you, saying, On day you go out and walk anywhere, know surely that dying you shall die? You said to me, Word I heard is good.

familiar.text: And the king sent and called for Shimei, and said unto him, Did I not make thee to swear by the LORD, and protested unto thee, saying, Know for a certain, on the day thou goest out, and walkest abroad any whither, that thou shalt surely die? and thou saidst unto me, The word that I have heard is good.

modern.text: the king summoned Shimei and said to him, “Did I not make you swear by the LORD and warn you, ‘On the day you leave and go elsewhere, know for sure that you will die’? And you told me, ‘The sentence is fair; I will comply.’

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ וַיִּקְרָ֣א לְשִׁמְעִ֗י וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו הֲל֧וֹא הִשְׁבַּעְתִּ֣יךָ בַֽיהוָ֗ה וָאָעִ֤ד בְּךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בְּי֣וֹם צֵאתְךָ֗ וְהָֽלַכְתָּ֙ אָ֣נֶה וָאָ֔נָה יָדֹ֥עַ תֵּדַ֖ע כִּ֣י מ֣וֹת תָּמ֑וּת וַתֹּ֧אמֶר אֵלַ֛י ט֥וֹב הַדָּבָ֖ר שָׁמָֽעְתִּי

verses.restored: Why then did you not guard oath of YHWH and command I commanded you?

familiar.text: Why then hast thou not kept the oath of the LORD, and the commandment that I have charged thee with?

modern.text: So why have you not kept your oath to the LORD and the command that I gave you?”

original.text: וּמַדּ֕וּעַ לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔רְתָּ אֵ֖ת שְׁבֻעַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וְאֶת הַמִּצְוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁר צִוִּ֥יתִי עָלֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: The king also said to Shimei, You know all evil your heart knows that you did to David my father. YHWH shall return your evil upon your head.

familiar.text: The king said moreover to Shimei, Thou knowest all the wickedness which thine heart is privy to, that thou didst to David my father: therefore the LORD shall return thy wickedness upon thine own head;

modern.text: The king also said, “You know in your heart all the evil that you did to my father David. Therefore the LORD will bring your evil back upon your head.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶל שִׁמְעִ֗י אַתָּ֤ה יָדַ֨עְתָּ֙ אֵ֣ת כָּל הָרָעָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָדַע֙ לְבָ֣בְךָ֔ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֖יתָ לְדָוִ֣ד אָבִ֑י וְהֵשִׁ֧יב יְהוָ֛ה אֶת רָעָתְךָ֖ בְּרֹאשֶֽׁךָ

verses.restored: But King Solomon shall be blessed, and throne of David shall be established before YHWH forever.

familiar.text: And king Solomon shall be blessed, and the throne of David shall be established before the LORD for ever.

modern.text: But King Solomon will be blessed and David’s throne will remain secure before the LORD forever.”

original.text: וְהַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בָּר֑וּךְ וְכִסֵּ֣א דָוִ֗ד יִהְיֶ֥ה נָכ֛וֹן לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה עַד עוֹלָֽם

verses.restored: The king commanded Benaiah son of Jehoiada. He went out, struck Shimei, and he died. The kingdom was established in hand of Solomon.

familiar.text: So the king commanded Benaiah the son of Jehoiada; which went out, and fell upon him, that he died. And the kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon.

modern.text: Then the king commanded Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he went out and struck Shimei down, and he died. Thus the kingdom was firmly established in the hand of Solomon.

original.text: וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֶת בְּנָיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן יְה֣וֹיָדָ֔ע וַיֵּצֵ֕א וַיִּפְגַּע בּ֖וֹ וַיָּמֹ֑ת וְהַמַּמְלָכָ֥ה נָכ֖וֹנָה בְּיַד שְׁלֹמֹֽה

translation_notes: David's command to 'be a man' reflects royal masculinity rhetoric. Courage, faithfulness, and maturity are not male monopolies and must not be taught through gender shame.
David leaves Solomon instructions that combine covenant obedience, patronage rewards, and delayed revenge. His oath not to kill Shimei personally is maneuvered around through the next king.
Abishag is discussed as a transferable dynastic asset; her desire is never recorded. Neither Adonijah, Bathsheba, nor Solomon has ethical authority to assign her marriage.

Adonijah, Joab, and Shimei are executed by royal order without a recorded public trial. Joab committed grave killings, but sanctuary execution and hereditary curse language remain ethically dangerous.
Abiathar's removal may be political accountability, dynastic consolidation, prophetic fulfillment, or all three. Prophecy must not erase human power analysis.
Shimei is subjected to indefinite geographic confinement and later executed after pursuing two escaped servants. The servants' flight and agency are not morally examined by the royal narrative.
Benaiah becomes the recurring executor and is rewarded with command. Institutional violence creates careers as well as corpses.
The repeated formula that the kingdom was established means consolidation through removal, banishment, surveillance, and death—not simply peaceful wisdom.
safety_note: Do not present Solomon's executions as automatically just because the narrative links them to wisdom, oath, prophecy, or dynastic peace. Do not treat Abishag as property, escaped servants as stolen objects, sanctuary as meaningless, masculinity as violence, or hereditary curses as ethical justice.
